channel.title: Adam Field's Blog
channel.description: Physics and mathematics blog by Adam Field: gravitational lensing, quantum field theory, wave equations, and computational astrophysics research notes.

item.title: FEMMI: Mass Map Inversion by Finite Elements and Boundary Integrals
item.description: A deep dive into FEMMI, my finite-element approach to weak-lensing mass reconstruction: why the boundary condition is the whole problem, why shear demands cubic P3 elements, how FEM-BEM coupling fixes the far field exactly, and how Morozov's principle removes the last free parameter.

item.title: Weak Lensing: Investigating Dark Matter in Galaxy Clusters
item.description: A companion blog to our undergraduate talk on weak gravitational lensing: covering dark matter motivation, the SuperBIT telescope, the full data pipeline from co-addition to mass reconstruction, and active research directions including ShearNet and FEMMI.

item.title: From Wavefunctions to Field Operators: The Necessity of Quantum Field Theory
item.description: Why single-particle quantum mechanics fails at high energies, and how promoting wavefunctions to field operators resolves the crisis. A rigorous bridge from Schrödinger to Klein-Gordon.

item.title: Weak Gravitational Lensing: From the Geodesic Equation to Mass Reconstruction
item.description: A rigorous derivation of weak gravitational lensing from first principles—starting with photon geodesics in curved spacetime and building to modern shear estimation techniques used in cosmological surveys.

item.title: Noether's Theorems: The Deep Connection Between Symmetry and Conservation
item.description: A rigorous derivation of Noether's first and second theorems from the calculus of variations, revealing how every continuous symmetry gives rise to a conserved quantity and connecting to gauge theories, quantum mechanics, and general relativity.

item.title: Deriving Schrödinger's Equation from First Principles
item.description: A rigorous derivation of Schrödinger's equation starting from Hamilton's optics-mechanics analogy, through the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, to the wave equation of quantum mechanics.

item.title: Solving the 1D Wave Equation: Classical and Transform Methods
item.description: Analytical solutions to the 1D wave equation via d'Alembert and Fourier–Laplace methods, with interactive visualization.

item.title: Solving the 2D Wave Equation: Separation of Variables and Mode Analysis
item.description: Analytical solution to the two-dimensional wave equation via separation of variables, with normal mode analysis and interactive visualization.

item.title: Deriving the Lorentz Force from First Principles
item.description: A complete derivation of F = q(E + v×B) using Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, showing how electromagnetic forces emerge from minimal coupling to gauge potentials.

item.title: Conservation of Energy: Why Δ(v²) ≠ (Δv)²
item.description: A rigorous demonstration of a common misconception in applying conservation of energy to moving particles.

item.title: Orthogonal Polynomials: From Theory to Your Name
item.description: A systematic derivation of orthogonal polynomials and their completeness, with an interactive tool to approximate your name using a complete set.

item.title: ShearNet: DeconvNet Development
item.description: Developing a secondary neural network for psf deconvolution from galaxy observations.

item.title: Part 1: My Main Research
item.description: Developing a neural network based solution for galaxy shear estimation

item.title: Part 2: ShearNet's Progress
item.description: My past and current work on ShearNet.
